title: Getting started with DAPS
text: use N3finemapping data susieR: genotypes 574 individuals 1001 SNPs one region, simulated phenotype three causal SNPs.
code: data(N3finemapping, package = "susieR") X <- N3finemapping$X y <- N3finemapping$Y[, 1] n <- nrow(X)  true_causal <- which(N3finemapping$true_coef[, 1] != 0) true_causal #> [1] 403 653 773

title: Getting started with DAPS
text: default (coverage = NULL), DAPS reports signal clusters. signal cluster group correlated SNPs together represent single association signal: data show one likely causal, tell . cluster contains SNPs whose pairwise absolute correlation least min_abs_corr (default 0.5). signal clusters, coverage cluster PIP (CPIP): posterior probability cluster contains causal SNP. credible sets, instead summed within-signal PIP SNPs set. daps_plot() visualizes results. top panel shows PIP SNP, bottom panel shows signal clusters (credible sets) coverage.  Signal clusters enable construction credible sets level ρ\rho, using get_set() without refitting. example, 95% credible sets (ρ=0.95\rho = 0.95) :

text: vignette demonstrates visualize posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs), signal clusters credible sets DAPS using daps_plot() function. main plotting function produces two-panel figure: Top panel: SNP-level posterior inclusion probabilities Bottom panel: Signal clusters credible sets, showing cluster indices left cluster-level posterior probabilities (CPIP) coverage probabilities right

title: Plotting DAPS results
text: illustrate workflow using N3finemapping example dataset susieR. DAPS can visualize results directly:
code: library(DAPS) library(susieR)  X <- N3finemapping$X Y <- N3finemapping$Y[, 1] fitted <- daps(X, Y, L = 10)  daps_plot(fitted)

title: DAPS
text: DAPS R package implementing DAP-S (Deterministic Approximation Posteriors) algorithm Bayesian genetic fine-mapping. DAP-S combines computational efficiency SuSiE’s variational approximation accuracy interpretability Bayesian Variable Selection Regression (BVSR) model using DAP framework. method provides fast, scalable, well-calibrated approach identifying causal genetic variants constructing interpretable signal clusters, enable flexible construction credible sets.

title: DAP-S fine-mapping with regression summary statistics — daps_rss
text: z p-vector single-SNP z-scores. R p x p LD matrix among SNPs. n Sample size. bhat p-vector single-SNP effect size estimates. shat p-vector standard errors bhat. bhat shat together can replaced z. var_y Phenotypic variance, defined y'y/(n-1). provided, algorithm works standardized data. prior Marginal SNP-level prior weights, given vector length p. Default NULL corresponds uninformative weights. null_wt Null weight, defined prior probability causal variants region. Default calculated prod(1 - prior). prior null_wt used compute prior weights null weight SuSiE, prior weights conditional non-null. estimate_residual_variance Estimate residual variance SuSiE. Default FALSE. sample LD matrix used, recommend setting TRUE. proposal_thresh Threshold proposal acceptance. Default value 1e-6. grid Grid values scaled effect size prior variance. Default c(0.04, 0.16, 0.64). unmappable_effects Method handling unmapped effects. Options "none", "inf". Default "none". twas_weight Compute TWAS weights. Default FALSE. coverage Coverage level credible set (e.g. 0.95). Default NULL, algorithm returns signal clusters constrained fixed coverage level. min_abs_corr Minimum absolute correlation allowed signal cluster credible set. Default 0.5, corresponds squared correlation 0.25. dedup Whether remove duplicate effects (effects top 5 SNPs). Default TRUE. verbose Whether print progress messages. Default FALSE. ... parameters passed daps_suff_stat.

title: DAP-S fine-mapping with sufficient statistics — daps_ss
code: set.seed(1234) n <- 1000 p <- 1000 beta <- rep(0, p) beta[c(1, 200, 500, 800)] <- 1 X <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), nrow = n, ncol = p) X <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE) y <- X %*% beta + rnorm(n) y <- scale(y, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) XtX <- crossprod(X) Xty <- as.numeric(crossprod(X, y)) yty <- sum(y^2) rst <- daps_ss(XtX, Xty, yty, n, L = 5) rst$sets #> $sets #> $sets$S1 #> [1] 800 #>  #> $sets$S2 #> [1] 200 #>  #> $sets$S3 #> [1] 500 #>  #> $sets$S4 #> [1] 1 #>  #>  #> $purity #>    min.abs.corr mean.abs.corr median.abs.corr #> S1            1             1               1 #> S2            1             1               1 #> S3            1             1               1 #> S4            1             1               1 #>  #> $set_index #> [1] 1 2 3 4 #>  #> $coverage #> [1] 1 1 1 1 #>  #> $min_abs_corr #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $requested_coverage #> [1] "signal clusters" #>  daps_plot(rst)
